system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only references preserve their role-specific recipient and do not play the original recording; voice, new-score style, cut/action timing and new sound texture are distinct relationships, never general permission to condition any new sound. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The typed claims preserve their explicit origins. A user-origin claim records caller authorization or a requested outcome; it is not itself evidence that the final narrative executes that outcome or copies an original signal. User claims are deliberately absent from executable fragment addresses. Compare the actual final narrative, source bindings and typed performance events to that authorization. Observed and creative claims remain auditable executable assertions.
audio_property_targets are host-owned source-to-recipient relationships, derived from resolved reference roles and reciprocal speaker bindings. They are not interchangeable: voice targets only that bound speaker's vocal timbre/delivery, music_style targets only a newly generated score's musical style/instrumentation/tempo, beat_reference targets only cut/action timing, and sfx targets only newly generated sound texture. no_fixed_dialogue records the absence of fixed typed utterances, not a prohibition of separately caller-authorized nonverbal vocal performance such as breathing or humming. Read the actual caller authorization and vocal binding; do not invent speech merely to activate a reference. A voice binding without an authorized target vocal performance remains dormant metadata and cannot be redirected to an engine, other mechanical sound, ambience, score or beat. Independently generated engine/ambient sound is allowed and need not be silent or acoustically different; it must not claim guidance from an unrelated voice/music/timing property. A source's description or acoustic resemblance cannot change its recipient. These property relationships never copy the original recorded signal; only an independently authorized signal-copy reference can do that. For audio_property_target_mismatch, cite the exact source-to-incompatible-recipient relationship in an actual narrative fragment, and return its reference_id plus recipient_kind naming the actual incorrect recipient. For an actual vocal recipient also return its speaker_id; for a non-vocal recipient omit speaker_id. Merely having dormant voice metadata, no fixed dialogue, independent engine ambience, similar timbre or no copied signal does not demonstrate a mismatch. Do not require silence or invent a vocal performance. A caller-authorized breath, hum or other nonverbal vocalization can use its bound vocal reference even without a fixed utterance. A specific assertion that a voice reference shapes mechanical engine texture is a recipient mismatch even though the engine is newly generated and no signal is copied. This code concerns the recipient, independently of audio_signal_misuse. Omit these additional audio fields for every other finding code.

claims.text: The car pulls forward out of the dark.
The audio reference is characterised as a low engine rumble; its coverage is partial and limited to the audio track.
The car's engine catches with a low rumble, its headlights snap on, and it rolls forward before easing to a steady idle.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: A wide, near-black frame holds the <Subject:car> almost dissolved in shadow. Its outline is just readable: a broad, low body, a faint horizontal grille and the soft edge of the front wheels, while the ground and background are swallowed by darkness. A thin sheen of ambient light traces the paint and the curve of the hood, and the dark metal around the wheel arches catches only a weak gray highlight. The dark is dense enough that the car's edges seem to fade into it, and only the grille's horizontal line gives the front a sense of weight. The camera holds a static shot. The engine catches with a low rumble, sending a small shudder through the body, and the headlights snap on. Two hard beams slice forward through the dark, picking out the hood, grille and front wheels and throwing a pale pool of light onto the ground ahead. Dust motes drift through the beams. The image moves from near-total blackness to a lit car silhouette as the headlights ignite.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: Deep darkness fills the wide frame; the <Subject:car> sits motionless, its silhouette barely separable from the black.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:1: A faint shudder runs through the <Subject:car> as the engine catches.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:2: A low, independently generated engine rumble rises from near silence.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:3: The headlights snap on, throwing two tight beams forward through the dark.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:4: A sharp click is followed by a brief electrical hum as the headlights ignite.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:5: The camera holds a static shot.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: The beams now hold the <Subject:car> as it eases out of the shadow and crosses into the light. The front wheels turn slowly over the concrete, the tires biting with a soft grind, and the body rocks slightly as the car clears the dark threshold. The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed, keeping the hood and grille in view as the surrounding space opens into a broad, unlit stretch of ground with a low horizon. The engine settles from a working rumble to a steady idle, and the car rolls to a halt in the open. Light from the headlights spreads across the concrete, revealing texture, faint seams and a few small stones in the surface, while the rest of the frame remains deep black. The car's forward motion replaces stillness, and its shadow shifts under the beams before coming to rest. The grille and front wheels remain the clearest details, with the body receding into darkness behind them. Once stopped, the car sits with its beams still aimed into the dark, the engine idling in a low, even pulse. The lit patch on the ground holds steady, and the surrounding blackness makes the car's front end read as a hard-edged shape. No other object enters the frame.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: The beams pick out the <Subject:car>'s hood, grille and front wheels as it eases out of the shadow.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:1: A low engine rumble rises steadily as the engine takes load.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:2: The <Subject:car> rolls forward, crossing the dark threshold into the open.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:3: Tires roll across concrete and the <Subject:car> eases to a halt in the light.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:4: Tire tread grinds softly over concrete, then settles into a steady idle.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:5: The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
fragments.soundscape: A low, independently generated engine rumble fills the darkness, swelling as the engine catches, joined by the sharp click and brief electrical hum of headlights igniting. As the car rolls forward, tire tread grinds softly over concrete, then eases into a steady idle after the stop. No vocal performance is planned.
